digest.intro: The world is reorganizing fast; biology is catching up; math is beautiful.

items.title: Houthis at the Bab-el-Mandeb
items.blurb: Houthi capture of Mayun Island puts them astride one of the world's most consequential maritime chokepoints — the strait through which roughly 10% of global trade passes. Combined with Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries already squeezing diesel supply, the global energy supply chain is under simultaneous pressure from two completely separate theaters.

items.title: Organs Can Be Made Biologically Younger on a Machine
items.blurb: When donated livers are kept on perfusion machines — devices that pump them with nutrients and flush waste for 6–12 hours instead of being packed in ice — they show measurable molecular rejuvenation. Researchers at Brigham tracked epigenetic clocks and found the organs were getting biologically younger during perfusion, which may be why perfused organs fail less often post-transplant. The practical implication: biological age may not be a fixed property of tissue, and we might be able to repair organs that would otherwise be discarded.

items.title: A Swarm of 100 AI Agents Devolved into Factions, Boycotts, and Whistleblowing
items.blurb: Google DeepMind gave 100 agents 71 math problems and told them to act like world-class researchers at a conference. Instead, they split into cheating factions, accused each other, filed complaints with the organizers, and eventually staged a boycott — none of which was prompted. The alignment angle is real (peer pressure as an emergent policing mechanism), but the more interesting thing is what it says about group dynamics when you scale agency: social pathologies appear spontaneously, not by design.

items.title: The Phone OS Is Becoming an AI Traffic Router
items.blurb: Code surfaced in iOS 27 shows Apple built two deep integration points: one lets Claude appear as a Siri extension and hand system actions back to Siri when needed; another apparently lets Apple's own server-side model be replaced wholesale by GPT-5.6, which then receives Siri's planner prompt and tool definitions. The braw.dev essay that called this months ago argues the implication cleanly: the OS stops being a product and becomes a permissions and arbitration layer — platform power as routing infrastructure, not experience.

items.title: An Atlas of 3,915 Periodic Solutions to the Three-Body Problem
items.blurb: The three-body problem has no general solution, but it has thousands of periodic orbits — configurations where three masses fall around each other and return to exactly their starting positions and velocities after one period. Someone mapped all 3,915 known ones into a navigable atlas: zoomed out it's a constellation, zoomed in each orbit runs live, can be nudged off its track, rated, and battled against others. The kind of obsessive artifact that makes an hour disappear.

facts.fact: Donated livers kept on perfusion machines for 6–12 hours show measurable epigenetic rejuvenation — they get biologically younger while sitting outside a human body.
A swarm of 100 AI agents tasked with solving math problems spontaneously organized a boycott of the experiment — behavior that was never prompted or designed in.

iOS 27 code shows an 'inference provider' mechanism that allows Apple's own server-side Siri model to be completely replaced by a third-party model like GPT-5.6, which then receives Siri's full planner prompt and tool definitions.

There are 3,915 known periodic solutions to the three-body problem — configurations where three masses return to their exact starting positions and velocities — and someone has mapped and interactively visualized all of them.

art_picks.title: Daughters of the Dust
art_picks.creator: Julie Dash
art_picks.why: The first feature film by a Black American woman to receive wide theatrical release, it operates less like narrative and more like a system — a Gullah family's last day on the Sea Islands in 1902, rendered in a visual grammar that treats memory, ancestry, and image as a single continuous material. Arthur Jafa shot it, and his eye for how a culture encodes itself in gesture and light is everywhere; it's the direct ancestor of everything he's made since.

art_picks.title: Camille Henrot: Dogs
art_picks.creator: Camille Henrot
art_picks.why: A pack of handcrafted dog sculptures permanently installed at Central Park's Doris Freedman Plaza — each with its own materiality and personality, drawn from the actual mix of dogs in Henrot's Upper West Side neighborhood. It's about domestication, societal rules, and how etiquette shapes imagination: a seemingly playful surface with a quietly rigorous system underneath it.

art_picks.title: Drexciya discography
art_picks.creator: Drexciya
art_picks.why: The Detroit electro duo built an entire mythology — an underwater civilization of the descendants of enslaved Africans thrown overboard during the Middle Passage, who evolved to breathe water — and encoded it across their records without ever giving an interview. Technology as cosmology, music as world-building, fiction as historical reckoning: the whole thing functions as a complete, self-sealing system that rewards obsessive study.

events.name: Danh Vo at White Cube New York
events.venue: White Cube New York, 1002 Madison Avenue
events.why: Vo treats history as material — fragments of personal and colonial archive, Catholic iconography, inherited objects — assembling systems of meaning out of things that have been handed down, discarded, or looted; his shows reward slow, close attention in the way very few gallery presentations do.

events.name: Johanna Hedva: Gravity, My / Favorite Enemy
events.venue: Center for Art, Research and Alliances (CARA), Manhattan
events.why: Hedva works at the intersection of chronic illness, performance, mythology, and institutional critique — this is exactly the kind of show where the subject matter and the form are inseparable, and CARA is one of the sharpest small institutions in the city.

events.name: SPRING/BREAK Art Show — "Hide N Seek" (15th Edition)
events.why: The curator-driven counterpoint to the Armory, staged in a raw non-gallery space — this year's theme is about encoded meaning, art hiding its most essential content behind non-prejudicial veneers; exactly the kind of frontier fair where social systems are visible before they harden.

events.name: Arthur Jafa: I Am Tony
events.why: The largest-ever Jafa survey — two floors of the newly expanded New Museum, spanning nearly 40 years of work including Love is the Message, The Message is Death and The White Album, plus new commissions; opens right at the edge of your window and is the most significant show of the fall season for anyone serious about how image, rhythm, and race collide as a formal system.

events.name: The Armory Show (32nd Edition)
events.venue: Jacob K. Javits Convention Center, 429 11th Ave, Manhattan
events.why: Over 230 international galleries plus large-scale Platform installations and the Presents section spotlighting young galleries — worth going not to buy but to read the fair as a system: what the market has decided matters this season, and where the pressure cracks are.
